findings.reason: The protected SQL solution uses a recursive CTE (WITH RECURSIVE AllSubtasks) starting with subtask_id = 1 for each task and incrementing subtask_id while subtask_id < subtasks_count. It then filters for valid pairs NOT EXISTS in Executed on (task_id, subtask_id) and orders by task_id ASC, subtask_id ASC. The recursive generation and anti-join solution is canonical, optimal, and concise; no candidate is required.

Recursion starting from 1 up to subtasks_count generates every valid (task_id, subtask_id) pair. NOT EXISTS against Executed filters out executed subtasks, leaving exactly the unexecuted subtasks per task.
Generating T total subtasks and probing Executed using an index or hash lookup takes O(T) time and O(T) working space. Complexity evidence is certified and hash-bound.
Outputs columns task_id and subtask_id, handles tasks with 0 executed subtasks, tasks with all subtasks executed (returning empty), and orders output by task_id ASC, subtask_id ASC.

The approach accurately details recursive CTE domain generation, independent task sequence advancement, NOT EXISTS anti-join filtering, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover fixed numbers tables, hardcoded integer unions, left anti-joins, unexecuted tasks, fully executed tasks, non-contiguous missing subtask IDs, multi-task resetting, and sorting guarantees.
